title: Rajasthan
region: The Land of Kings · North-West India
description: No place in India wears its history as grandly as Rajasthan. Hilltop forts guard every city — Amber above Jaipur, Mehrangarh over the blue houses of Jodhpur, the golden citadel of Jaisalmer rising from the Thar Desert — and palaces seem to float on the lakes of Udaipur.

Between them lie holy Pushkar, the havelis of Bikaner, tigers in Ranthambhore and nights under the stars at the Sam sand dunes, with camel rides, folk music and some of the country's richest food and crafts along the way.

highlights.title: Forts of the desert kings
highlights.text: Amber, Mehrangarh, Junagarh and the living fort of Jaisalmer — still home to thousands of residents.

highlights.title: Udaipur's lake palaces
highlights.text: The City Palace and Jag Mandir, best seen from a boat on Lake Pichola as the sun goes down.

highlights.title: Thar Desert nights
highlights.text: Camel rides, folk dances and tent stays on the Sam sand dunes outside Jaisalmer.

highlights.title: Bazaars & crafts
highlights.text: Block prints, blue pottery, mirror work and silver in the colourful markets of Jaipur and Jodhpur.
